name: Regal Empire Standard Calendar
description: 12 months, 365 days, 7 weekdays. BF counts UP toward the present — 722 BF is oldest dated record, 1040 BF is current game date. Larger year = closer to now. Think 'pages in a chronicle' not 'countdown'.
bfMeaning: BF is the in-world chronicle designation. Waluigi translates it as 'Before Fracture' in footnotes, but the annalists filed it as sequential — earliest entry is 722 BF, present is 1040 BF, so year numbers increase toward now. Intuition: It's a log number, not a countdown.
note: Deepwinter has 35 days to make 365. Rest days are Venerias and Saturias.
pocketClocksNote: A pocket clock is a place whose year is STUCK while the party lives through it. Its filings are PRESENT-TENSE SESSIONS, not flashbacks or recovered history — the low year number describes where the room is, not when the reading happened. Never sort a pocket-clock filing into the archive's past, and never date one by walking back from currentDate.json: chain it against the prior session on ITS OWN clock. The Material Plane clock in currentDate.json keeps running the whole time.

pocketClocks.name: The Feyward clock
pocketClocks.realm: Feywild — the Feyward manor and the Eternal Bloom around it
pocketClocks.heldBy: Lady Aurelian, who is attempting to lock her own timeline down rather than let the Planar Fracture take it
pocketClocks.summary: Feyward is not a memory the party is reading. It is a room they are standing in, and the room's year stopped. Sessions filed on the Feyward clock are happening NOW in session order, concurrently with Material Plane sessions dated 1040 BF. The party walks between the two and the numbers do not reconcile; that is the horror of the place, not a filing error.
pocketClocks.filingRule: Date on the Feyward clock, always with the '(Feyward clock)' qualifier, and chain forward from the previous Feyward session. Do not convert to a Material date. Do not label it 'historical', 'recovered', 'backfilled' or 'flashback'.
pocketClocks.materialConcurrency: Feyward sessions play alongside the Material present. Where a filing needs to state both, write the Feyward date first and note the Material standing in the same line.

deadlinesNote:
A deadline is an in-world timer that is RUNNING. It is not flavour: when it reaches zero the stated consequence happens. Deadlines are declared here so the site can render them and so no filing has to re-derive the arithmetic.

Remaining time is DERIVED, never stored. It is measured from the deadline's own clock: the site finds the newest filed session on `clock`, reads its in-world date, and subtracts. That is why the countdown falls on its own every time a session on that clock is filed — nobody has to remember to decrement a counter, and the clock can never disagree with the filings. `startedOn` is the moment the timer began and must not be moved.

deadlines.name: The Feyward tether cut
deadlines.summary: The Oracle gives Bowser three weeks before he manually cuts the planar tether joining the Feyward to the Material sanctum. Bowser talked him up from one week and asked twice not to have it cut exactly on the mark.
deadlines.consequence: The planar tether between the Feyward and the Material sanctum is severed, closing the route between the Feyward party and the sanctum.
deadlines.grace: Bowser twice asked that it not be cut exactly at three weeks and was hinted at a margin. The agreed figure is a hard 21 days; any grace is the Oracle's to give and is not promised.
deadlines.rewardIfMet: Three unnamed rewards: one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, and one Bowser said he wanted today.
deadlines.note: The countdown started on Bowser's teleport into the basement, not on the handshake. It falls by itself as Feyward sessions are filed, because the remaining time is measured against the newest Feyward filing's own date and hour. Bowser's bargain is the term; the Soul-Ring session is where the upstairs party first hears the same twenty-one days, from Brad in the goblin card room, as a rumour of the world ending. They know the number and not that anyone negotiated it, and they do not know it was Bowser who bought the other two weeks.
deadlines.startedOnNote: The teleport hour is not stated outright. The only clock reading in the basement is the goblin's 'maybe like 2 am', and it lands midway through Bowser's time down there — after the altar, the hall, the failed lockpick, the cold storage and Mystic Morel, before the satyr and the cards. Everything he does in that cellar is one short sequence, so arrival is placed half an hour earlier at 01:30 rather than padding it out. The term is counted from there and reads thirty minutes short.
